Kenosha Will O' The Wisp
BILLY WOOD
Billy Wood has been racing
midget automobiles for about 15
years. In that time he has won
the Badger Midget Racing asso-
ciation championship six times
and has scored many wins in
United States Auto Club midget
auto events, driving a number
of cars including one owned by
Harry Turner, veteran Kenosha
driver and owner. Wood, who
weighs 150 pounds or so, has the
reputation as a "charger" who
puts the throttle to the floor and
ARMY KRUEGER PHOTO
keeps it there from the start to the finish of any race. When not racing, the 35 year old Kenosha thin man
works in the trim department at American Motors Corp.

Defending Midget Champ
RONNIE ERFURTH
A number of years ago Ron
Erfurth was seriously injured in
a midget auto race. There was
some question that he might not
pull through . .. let alone drive
again. But the powerfully built
blonde speedster from Oregon,
Wis. did come back all the way,
winning the Badger Midget Rac-
ing season's championship in
1964. And he did it against some
of the finest competition the as-
sociation has fielded in its 27
years of existence. Erfurth won
ARMY KRUEGER PHOTO
five features last year on his way to the title and ranks among the top five this year. He drives one of the
